objectives.text: Use the African Union chair and the Luanda process to make Angola the broker of Central Africa's wars. President Lourenco chaired the AU in 2025. Angola ran the DRC-Rwanda talks from the 2022 Luanda Roadmap and in March 2025 announced it was stepping back as mediator to focus on the AU presidency. It tried to return in February 2026 with a ceasefire proposal that the M23 rejected.

constraints.text: Fuel subsidies meet the street. The fuel price rise of 1 July 2025 set off a minibus taxi stoppage that became looting and clashes in Luanda and other cities; the presidency reported 22 dead, 197 injured and 1,214 arrests. Subsidy reform, begun in 2023, has a visible political price.

paradoxes.text: The corridor that is meant to bring Angola Western money and a regional role runs into the DRC mining belt, where the war is. Luanda gave up the DRC mediator's chair in March 2025, the same spring the Lobito financing was being settled, so the state that wants to pacify the mining region is also its railway partner.

grand_strategy.reading: Angola's grand strategy is to turn oil money and a continental chair into a regional and Western role while the Chinese loans of the last two decades are paid down. Its tools are the AU presidency, the Luanda venue and the Lobito corridor, and its limits are the oil output that fell from 1.42 to 1.1 million barrels a day and the 2025 fuel riots, which show how little room subsidy reform has. Not verified in this pass: the Soviet-era legacy and the cooling with Moscow, the 2027 succession, the Trump-era posture beyond the Lobito funding, the Zambian trend (the ZMB card reads warming, not carried here), and diamonds as an export, all of which need their own sources.

stances.note: Lobito corridor money kept flowing under Trump: US officials said in April 2025 the US remained committed despite spending cuts, and the DFC signed a USD 553m loan on 17 December 2025 (Biden's 2024 pledge delivered). Early 2025 was shaky: USAID-linked funds were frozen in February. Transactional infrastructure cooperation with no alignment: partner. Trend stable is our reading (the funding held through the freeze scare). Bond none is our reading; no source names kinship or grievance. Gap: the 2025 Trump-era posture beyond the Lobito funding and any US security ties are not researched; the USA card is not yet mirrored.

stances.note: China is the largest creditor and buyer of Angolan oil: oil-backed debt fell by almost a quarter in 2025 to about USD 7.7bn (from 10.1bn), and Luanda has been reducing its exposure to resource-backed loans. Cooling is our reading from that repayment and the stated wish to borrow less against oil. The February 2026 Sonangol request for a USD 4.8bn Chinese refinery loan is a counter-signal, so the trend is only cooling on the debt, not on the relationship. Transactional, no alignment: partner. Bond none is our reading. Gap: the 2025 finance-ministry figure comes from secondary reporting and the original Reuters interview was not read.
